item.title: Chrome V8 Zero-Day, WordPress Plugin RCE Exploitation, and Toy Ghouls Backdoors
item.content:encoded:
Window: 04 Sep 06:06 → 04 Sep 11:06 UTC (5 hours)

Google Releases Chrome Update to Patch Actively Exploited V8 Zero-Day — Must Read

Google released Chrome updates to fix CVE-2026-85046, an actively exploited high-severity V8 type confusion zero-day that can allow arbitrary code execution via a crafted HTML page. Users should update Chrome and other Chromium-based browsers as fixes become available.

  • Google released security updates for Chrome to patch 12 vulnerabilities, including an actively exploited zero-day.
  • The actively exploited flaw is CVE-2026-85046, a high-severity type confusion bug in Chrome’s V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine with a CVSS score of 8.8.
  • CVE-2026-85046 could allow a remote attacker to execute arbitrary code inside the Chrome sandbox using a crafted HTML page.
  • Security researcher Salvatore Gulizia reported the flaw on August 4, 2026 and described it as a V8 compiler bug that can be turned into arbitrary read and write access on the JavaScript heap.
  • Users are advised to update Chrome to versions 152.0.7977.82/.83 for Windows and macOS and 152.0.7977.82 for Linux, while users of other Chromium-based browsers should apply fixes when available.

Technologies: browser

Products: google-chrome, v8, microsoft-edge, brave-browser, opera-browser, vivaldi-browser, chromium

Vendors: google, microsoft, brave-software, opera, vivaldi-technologies

Over 440,000 Exploit Attempts Target Super Forms and Elementor Pro RCE Flaws — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting critical arbitrary file upload flaws in the Super Forms and Elementor Pro WordPress plugins to plant PHP web shells and potentially take over sites. Site owners should update to the fixed versions immediately and check for suspicious recently modified PHP files.

  • Threat actors are exploiting two critical security flaws in the WordPress plugins Super Forms and Elementor Pro, according to Wordfence.
  • CVE-2026-14894 in Super Forms allows unauthenticated attackers to upload files of any type, including executable PHP files, leading to remote code execution, and it was fixed in version 6.3.314.
  • CVE-2026-32475 in Elementor Pro allows unauthenticated attackers to upload files of any type, including executable PHP files, leading to remote code execution, and it was fixed in version 4.2.2.
  • Wordfence said it has blocked over 250,000 exploit attempts targeting CVE-2026-14894 and over 190,000 exploit attempts targeting CVE-2026-32475.
  • WordPress site owners using the two plugins are advised to apply patches immediately, scan for indicators of compromise, and audit for unexpected or recently modified .php files.

Technologies: cms

Products: super-forms-drag-drop-form-builder, elementor-pro, wordpress

Vendors: wordfence, patchstack, elementor, wordpress

Angry Birds: Toy Ghouls’ new toys — Should Read

Kaspersky reports that the financially motivated Toy Ghouls group has added custom backdoors to its arsenal, using HiveMQ MQTT and Matrix/Element as command-and-control channels. The shift from public tools to custom malware suggests the group is becoming more sophisticated and harder to detect.

  • Kaspersky observed Toy Ghouls using a custom backdoor for the first time in early July 2026 after previously relying on public GitHub tools, leaked Babuk and LockBit ransomware builders, and later its own GenieLocker ransomware.
  • The researchers identified two versions of the backdoor: mqtt-bird-agent 0.1.0, which uses the HiveMQ MQTT broker as its command-and-control server, and matrix-bird-agent 0.1.0, which relies on the Element messenger.
  • The attackers deliver the backdoors and their configuration files to compromised systems using Windows Remote Management with open-source tools such as Evil-WinRM and WinRM-fs.
  • Both backdoor versions can establish persistence as Windows services, encrypt or store configuration data tied to the infected machine, and stop running if the configuration cannot be decrypted.
  • The backdoors collect system status and metrics, receive remote commands, execute them through PowerShell or the Windows command line, and send command results back through HiveMQ or Matrix/Element channels.

Technologies: message-queue, remote-access, operating-system

Products: hivemq-mqtt-broker, element, windows-remote-management, powershell, windows

Vendors: hivemq, element, microsoft, kaspersky

A Phishing Kit Padded Its Payload With Someone Else's Mail — Should Read

A credential-phishing email passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication by using controlled or repurposed infrastructure, then hid a malicious settlement-agreement link behind an ESP tracker. Its key evasion tactic was padding the short lure with a stolen legitimate commercial email to make the message look statistically normal to scanners while keeping the real phish visible to the victim.

  • A fully authenticated phishing email reached two mailboxes at a food service packaging manufacturer with SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication all passing.
  • The visible lure was a four-line settlement approval message using the recipient’s first name, full email address, and company name, with a single link disguised as a signer approval settlement agreement PDF.
  • The link used a Mandrill click tracking URL that relayed to a credential page on secure.individual-elegance.co.za, which the platform scored as malicious.
  • The email’s HTML contained roughly seventy blank line breaks followed by a complete, unrelated legitimate commercial email that had been sent to a different person at a different organization.
  • Themis flagged the message as credential theft with 89% confidence, and both affected mailboxes were quarantined and mitigated.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: themis, ironscales-platform, amazon-ses, mandrill, dynamics-365

Vendors: ironscales, amazon-web-services, mailchimp, microsoft

Plex Urges Immediate Updates After Patching Multiple Undisclosed Security Flaws — Should Read

Plex is urging users to immediately update Plex Media Server to 1.43.3 and Plex Desktop to 1.115.0 after patching multiple undisclosed security flaws. The company has not shared technical details yet, but CVEs have been requested and exposed Plex servers have been targeted in past attacks.

  • Plex is urging users to update to Plex Media Server 1.43.3 and Plex Desktop 1.115.0 after releasing fixes for multiple security flaws.
  • Plex did not provide details about the newly patched issues but said CVE identifiers have been requested for them.
  • Plex said NAS users may need to install the updated Plex Media Server package manually if it is not yet available through their package manager.
  • In August 2025, Plex addressed CVE-2025-34158, a high-severity authentication bug that could expose a server owner’s account details and administrative access token to lower-privileged authenticated users.
  • Censys data shows more than 360,000 devices exposing the Plex Media Server web interface, although not all of them are vulnerable.

Products: plex-media-server, plex-desktop

Vendors: plex

GPT-6 Astra Scores 100% on ExploitBench as OpenAI Blocks PoC Exploit Requests — Should Read

OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra, a frontier AI model that scored 100% on ExploitBench but is being released with safeguards that block proof-of-concept exploit generation. The company says it will initially focus access on defensive uses like secure code review and patching, with expanded capabilities planned through its Daybreak program.

  • OpenAI officially unveiled GPT-6 Astra, describing it as the world's most intelligent and aligned model.
  • OpenAI said GPT-6 Astra reached the Critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework and scored 100% on ExploitBench, compared with 78.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol.
  • OpenAI said the released version of Astra is limited to secure code review and patching and refuses prompts related to creating proof-of-concept exploits for vulnerabilities.
  • OpenAI plans to expand access through OpenAI Daybreak to enable more defensive workflows, including vulnerability and proof-of-concept validation, malware analysis, and detection engineering.
  • OpenAI launched Daybreak for Frontline Defenders, a $1 billion global project to help critical infrastructure sectors and resource-limited organizations use frontier AI cyber capabilities to protect essential services.

Technologies: cloud-platform

item.title: Exchange CVE-2026-62911 Exposure and AI-Assisted Vulnerability Defense Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Sep 18:00 → 03 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Microsoft Exchange Vulnerability CVE-2026-62911: What Administrators Should Do and How Zscaler Can Help — Should Read

Microsoft patched CVE-2026-62911, a high-severity Exchange Server authentication bypass that can let a low-privileged attacker take over all mailboxes, but thousands of internet-exposed servers remain unpatched and public exploit code exists. Administrators should patch immediately or remove Exchange from direct internet access, with the article recommending Zscaler’s zero-trust access controls as a way to reduce exposure.

  • Microsoft’s August 2026 Patch Tuesday included a fix for CVE-2026-62911, a high-severity authentication bypass vulnerability affecting Exchange Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition.
  • Shadowserver identified around 22,000 Exchange servers that remained unpatched and exposed to the internet as of September 1, including roughly 6,200 in the United States and 5,100 in Germany.
  • Microsoft said successful exploitation of CVE-2026-62911 allows an attacker with basic privileges to take over all mailboxes on the targeted server, including reading and sending email and downloading attachments.
  • The Netherlands National Cyber Security Centre confirmed that working exploit code for CVE-2026-62911 is already publicly available.
  • The article recommends applying the August 2026 update immediately, and if patching is delayed, ensuring the Exchange server is not reachable from the open internet.

Technologies: remote-access, dlp, cloud-platform

Products: exchange-server-2016, exchange-server-2019, exchange-server-subscription-edition, zscaler-private-access, zpa-clientless-access, zscaler-data-security, zscaler-deception, zscaler-cloud-workload-segmentation, appshield, microsoft-365, mythos

Vendors: microsoft, zscaler, anthropic

Introducing context-aware vulnerability discovery and remediation with Cloudflare Managed Defense and OpenAI Daybreak models — Optional

Cloudflare is launching early access to Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation, a Managed Defense service that uses OpenAI Daybreak models to find, validate, prioritize, and propose fixes for vulnerabilities in customer-authorized code. The key value is combining source-code analysis with Cloudflare production traffic, WAF, and security-event context so teams can focus first on exposed, actively targeted issues while retaining control over any patches or rules.

  • Cloudflare announced early access to Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation, an invitation-only service within Cloudflare Managed Defense that helps customers detect and mitigate vulnerabilities in authorized codebases.
  • The service uses OpenAI Daybreak models, including GPT-5.6 Cyber, for reconnaissance, hunting, and validation, while customers decide whether proposed code patches or mitigations are implemented.
  • Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation combines source code analysis with Cloudflare Web Assets, WAF, Workers Observability, and traffic and security data to prioritize findings based on production exposure and security activity.
  • The system can recommend code patches and, when evidence supports it, Cloudflare WAF Custom rules scoped around the method, path, and request details needed to reach vulnerable code.
  • Model prompts are sent from Cloudflare Workers through Cloudflare AI Gateway to OpenAI servers, and no model inference runs at Cloudflare's edge or can directly apply patches or rules.

Technologies: waf, cloud-platform, api-gateway

Products: cloudflare-managed-defense, vulnerability-discovery-and-remediation, daybreak-defense-network, gpt-5-6-cyber, cloudflare-waf, cloudflare-workers, web-assets, workers-observability, cloudflare-ai-gateway, workers-trace-events-logpush

Vendors: cloudflare, openai

The story behind the intelligence — Optional

Cisco Talos warns that AI model guardrails are increasingly blocking legitimate security work, creating a “safety penalty” that slows defenders while attackers use less-restricted tools. Security teams should measure AI refusal rates and plan fallback or private AI options to preserve incident-response capability.

  • The newsletter emphasizes that producing usable threat intelligence involves messy investigative work, including dead ends, conversations, and evidence-gathering that are usually abstracted away from the final product.
  • Talos researcher Azim Khodjibaev’s adversary engagement work includes developing deep- and dark-web personas, directly engaging threat actors, and maintaining relationships with people who have openly threatened him.
  • Khodjibaev has maintained eight separate personas at once, some of which interacted with one another, and his engagements have helped Talos identify prolific cybercriminals and support wider disruption efforts.
  • Cisco Talos describes an AI “safety penalty,” where built-in guardrails in frontier AI models increasingly block legitimate defensive tasks and can delay incident response.
  • Talos recommends that security leaders audit AI refusal rates and evaluate alternatives such as private infrastructure, Model-as-a-Service platforms, or hybrid fallback systems that reroute refused prompts to an unconstrained local model.

Technologies: identity-provider

Products: claude, chatgpt, reddit, roblox, papercut, okta-single-sign-on

Vendors: cisco, hugging-face, anthropic, openai, reddit, roblox, papercut, okta

item.title: ShinyHunters Health Vishing, Blockchain WebRTC Malware, Azure Privilege Escalation, MECCHA RCE
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Sep 14:00 → 03 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Urgent Threat Alert: ShinyHunters Vishing Campaigns and Domain Impersonation — Must Read

Health-ISAC warns that ShinyHunters is actively targeting global healthcare organizations with vishing and lookalike domains to steal SSO credentials and bypass MFA. Organizations should urgently block suspicious .claim/.claims domains, harden MFA and helpdesk workflows, monitor impersonation infrastructure, and restrict access to verified corporate devices.

  • Health-ISAC warns that ShinyHunters is actively targeting the global health sector with persistent, highly targeted voice phishing campaigns using malicious medical-themed impersonation domains.
  • The campaigns attempt to trick employees into entering credentials on fake login pages and have succeeded in some recent cases by bypassing multi-factor authentication.
  • After compromising an identity, the actors rapidly pivot from single sign-on platforms into connected SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, and Salesforce to exfiltrate data and internal communications.
  • Observed impersonation domains commonly use the target company’s name followed by patterns such as company-claims.com or company.claims.
  • Health-ISAC recommends blocking .claim and .claims domains unless legitimate, improving employee awareness, enforcing device-context verification, adopting phishing-resistant MFA, hardening helpdesk and MFA reset workflows, and monitoring lookalike infrastructure.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa, cloud-platform

Products: microsoft-365, sharepoint, salesforce

Vendors: microsoft, salesforce

Malware on the Blockchain: An Ongoing Campaign’s New WebRTC Twist — Must Read

Netskope found an ongoing EtherHiding campaign using BNB Smart Chain testnet contracts to deliver payloads through more than 5,400 compromised small-business websites. A newer variant replaces the usual ClickFix lure with a covert WebRTC data-channel stager that bypasses normal signaling and pulls executable code directly from attacker-controlled infrastructure.

  • Netskope observed more than 5,400 compromised small-business websites making JSON-RPC calls to BNB Smart Chain testnet endpoints to retrieve payloads from a smart contract.
  • The compromised sites, often WordPress and sometimes PrestaShop, carried an injected loader as either an inline script or a spoofed package, but the initial compromise method is unknown.
  • The common delivery chain retrieves a second-stage script from the blockchain that displays a ClickFix lure instructing visitors to paste and run a command that downloads the final payload.
  • A newer variant delivers a WebRTC data-channel stager that hand-writes its own session answer to open an encrypted UDP channel to the attacker without normal signaling traffic.
  • The WebRTC stager buffers code received from the command channel and executes it in the browser by injecting a script into the page, reusing an existing Content Security Policy nonce when available.

Technologies: cms

Products: bnb-smart-chain, bsc-testnet, wordpress, prestashop, powershell

Vendors: netskope, bnb-chain, wordpress, prestashop, microsoft

Modern Adventures in Azure Privilege Escalation — Should Read

Azure privilege escalation analysis should focus on individual RBAC permissions and ABAC conditions, not just role names, because built-in and custom roles can hide dangerous paths. Using this approach, the researchers found and Microsoft fixed a built-in Anyscale role that could allow escalation to Owner via unconstrained role assignments.

  • Azure’s growth to more than 200 services, 897 built-in RBAC roles, and 22,018 permissions has expanded the Azure attack surface and made privilege escalation mapping more complex.
  • The article argues that reviewing individual Azure RBAC permissions, along with ABAC conditions, gives a more thorough view of privilege escalation paths than reviewing role names alone.
  • Azure ABAC conditions are used heavily in built-in roles, especially around Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, to constrain which role assignments a principal can create or delete.
  • The 2023-07-01-preview version of the Azure Role Definitions List API can filter roles by specified permissions and help map dangerous permissions to built-in and custom roles.
  • The researchers found that the built-in Anyscale Platform Administrator Role had unconstrained role assignment write and delete permissions, and Microsoft later removed those permissions after the issue was reported to MSRC.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, identity-provider, secrets-manager, object-storage

Products: microsoft-azure, azure-rbac, azure-resource-manager, azure-portal, azure-key-vault, azure-storage-accounts, azure-machine-learning, microsoft-entra-id, anyscale-platform

Vendors: microsoft, anyscale, netspi

MECCHA CHAMELEON can't hide from the RCE — May Read

Researchers found that malicious MECCHA CHAMELEON custom maps could abuse Unreal Engine audio recording functions to write attacker-controlled files to a victim’s Windows Startup folder, enabling delayed remote code execution after reboot. The issue was reported to the developers and patched in version 4.0.0.

  • Researchers found that MECCHA CHAMELEON custom maps could abuse the exposed Unreal Engine function StopRecordingOutput to write files to arbitrary locations on a victim’s filesystem.
  • The attack worked because maps can contain Unreal Engine Blueprints that run inside the MECCHA CHAMELEON process when a map is loaded.
  • The proof of concept wrote a file into the Windows Startup folder so it would execute after the victim’s system restarted.
  • The researchers used a null character in the filename to bypass Unreal Engine’s automatic .wav suffix and created an HTA payload inside an uncompressed PCM WAV recording.
  • The developers fixed the vulnerability in MECCHA CHAMELEON 4.0.0 by preventing StopRecordingOutput from creating files, and the update is installed automatically before launching the game.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: meccha-chameleon, unreal-engine, steam-workshop, microsoft-windows, mshta

Vendors: microsoft, epic-games, valve

item.title: NetSPI-Synack Merge as ESP Invoice Fraud and Anti-Bot Bypasses Surface
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Sep 10:00 → 03 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Invoice Scam That Came With an Unsubscribe Link — Should Read

Attackers used a legitimate company’s compromised bulk-mail account to send an invoice-fraud email that passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and included a real unsubscribe link, making it look like normal compliant marketing mail. The key warning is that authentication and bulk-mail compliance prove the sending route, not that a payment request is legitimate, so money-transfer instructions still need out-of-band verification.

  • An invoice-fraud email reached a regional financial-advisory firm through an unrelated company’s legitimate marketing-list account, with passing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and a working one-click unsubscribe footer.
  • The message used a fabricated email thread impersonating a named advisor at the recipient’s firm to pressure a payment approver to settle an invoice without delay.
  • The email body contained a U+200C zero-width non-joiner between every letter, making the text render normally while defeating literal keyword and phrase matching.
  • The message included two divergent reply addresses on unrelated domains, including one on the attacker-registered domain azurecloudemailus[.]com.
  • IRONSCALES Themis flagged the message based on relationship context, including a visible sender name matching a known internal contact whose real address was on a different domain.

Technologies: email-security

Products: themis

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

While anti-bot vendors talk about AI agents, classical bots are getting the bypasses — Optional

The article argues that anti-bot vendors are over-focusing on AI agent “intent” while traditional bots are still successfully bypassing defenses through reverse engineering, browserless solvers, and valid anti-bot payload generation. The key test remains whether a product can reliably detect automation when attackers understand and reproduce the signals it trusts.

  • The article argues that anti-bot vendors are increasingly focused on AI agent management even though traditional bot detection and anti-abuse problems remain unsolved.
  • The author says major anti-bot systems are being reverse engineered and bypassed, including through browserless solvers that reproduce expected signals without running protected JavaScript in a real browser.
  • The article states that AI can help attackers analyze undocumented public APIs, inspect and deobfuscate anti-bot JavaScript, debug automation, reproduce expected signals, and maintain tooling when targets change.
  • The author argues that real-world abuse such as credential stuffing, fake account creation, and emergency fraud rules is easier to measure than vague claims about understanding an AI agent’s intent.
  • The article concludes that anti-bot products should be judged by whether they can reliably identify automation when attackers understand and try to reproduce the signals the defenses trust.

Technologies: browser

Products: playwright, perplexity-comet, claude, camoufox, cloakbrowser, roxybrowser

Vendors: microsoft, perplexity, anthropic, camoufox, cloakbrowser, roxybrowser, forrester

A New Era for Offensive Security — Optional

NetSPI and Synack are merging with backing from KKR to form a larger offensive security platform. The companies say their approach will combine AI-enabled testing with human expert judgment, arguing that fully autonomous pentesting alone misses complex, business-specific risks.

  • NetSPI and Synack announced a definitive agreement to merge, backed by KKR, to form what they describe as a leading offensive cybersecurity platform.
  • The companies say they bring nearly 40 years of combined operating history and more than 13 million hours of real-world offensive testing experience.
  • The article argues that fully autonomous testing falls short because sophisticated vulnerabilities can depend on business logic, infrastructure choices, and attacker creativity.
  • NetSPI and Synack state that AI is most powerful when combined with expert judgment to accelerate discovery, analysis, and validation of findings.
  • The combined company plans to offer continuous security testing and validation across the full attack surface, expanded service offerings, and greater operational scale.

Vendors: netspi, synack

item.title: Supply Chain Risk Focus: MOVEit CVE-2023-34362 and Vendor Breach Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 03 Sep 06:00 → 03 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Supply Chain Attacks in 2026: Why Threat Intelligence Is the Only Early Warning System That Works — Optional

Supply chain attacks are now a major breach vector because trusted vendors, software components, and managed platforms can be compromised outside an organization’s direct visibility. The article argues that continuous external threat intelligence and vendor monitoring are necessary to detect these risks before they become public breaches.

  • Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found third-party involvement in 48% of breaches, up 60% year over year.
  • The article says supply chain attacks target vendors, software components, and build pipelines that an organization depends on, rather than attacking the organization directly.
  • CISA and the FBI documented that the Cl0p ransomware group exploited CVE-2023-34362 in Progress Software's MOVEit Transfer platform beginning on May 27, 2023.
  • By January 2024, breaches or downstream exposures linked to MOVEit affected more than 2,700 organizations and compromised personal data of more than 93 million people, according to tracking by Emsisoft and KonBriefing Research.
  • The article argues that continuous monitoring of vendor infrastructure, exposed credentials, dark web chatter, and third-party breach signals is needed because traditional vulnerability management does not cover those external risks.

Products: moveit-transfer, goanywhere-mft, cyble-third-party-risk-management

Vendors: progress-software, fortra, cyble

MECCHA CHAMELEON can't hide from the RCE — Should Read

Researchers found a patched MECCHA CHAMELEON custom-map vulnerability that let malicious Steam Workshop maps write arbitrary files to a player’s Windows system, enabling delayed code execution on restart. The issue was fixed in version 4.0.0, and players are advised to be cautious with unofficial maps.

Modern Adventures in Azure Privilege Escalation — Should Read

NetSPI shows that Azure privilege escalation mapping should focus on individual RBAC permissions and ABAC conditions, not just role names, because built-in and custom roles can hide powerful escalation paths. Using this approach, researchers found and reported an Azure built-in Anyscale Platform Administrator role that could assign arbitrary roles and escalate to Owner before Microsoft removed the dangerous permissions.

  • Azure’s attack surface has grown with more than 200 services, 897 built-in Azure RBAC roles, and 22,018 different permissions as of June 2026.
  • The article argues that mapping privilege escalation techniques to individual Azure RBAC permissions provides a more thorough review of escalation paths than focusing only on roles.
  • Azure ABAC conditions are increasingly used in built-in roles to constrain privileged actions such as Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, but those conditions must be reviewed alongside RBAC role assignments to understand effective permissions.
  • NetSPI found that the built-in Anyscale Platform Administrator Role contained Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write and Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete without ABAC conditions, allowing arbitrary privilege escalation to Owner before Microsoft removed those permissions.
  • The article recommends that Azure administrators review every role for unexpected permissions, follow least privilege, reduce use of highly privileged roles, and assign roles at the narrowest possible scope.

The Invoice Scam That Came With an Unsubscribe Link — Should Read

Attackers used a legitimate company’s compromised bulk-mail account to send an invoice-fraud email that passed SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and included a real unsubscribe link, making it look like normal compliant marketing mail. The key warning is that authentication and bulk-mail compliance prove the sending route, not that a payment request is legitimate, so money-transfer instructions still need out-of-band verification.

  • An invoice-fraud email reached a regional financial-advisory firm through an unrelated company’s legitimate marketing-list account, with passing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC and a working one-click unsubscribe footer.
  • The message used a fabricated email thread impersonating a named advisor at the recipient’s firm to pressure a payment approver to settle an invoice without delay.
  • The email body contained a U+200C zero-width non-joiner between every letter, making the text render normally while defeating literal keyword and phrase matching.
  • The message included two divergent reply addresses on unrelated domains, including one on the attacker-registered domain azurecloudemailus[.]com.
  • IRONSCALES Themis flagged the message based on relationship context, including a visible sender name matching a known internal contact whose real address was on a different domain.

Technologies: email-security

Remote access hardening playbook: Reducing RMM tool risk for SMBs — Optional

SMBs and MSPs should reduce remote access risk by inventorying and consolidating RMM tools, blocking attacker-favored tools like MeshAgent and Ammyy Admin unless explicitly authorized, and hardening legitimate tools with MFA, patching, application control, and monitoring for unauthorized installs or suspicious lateral movement.

  • Acronis telemetry from over 1.8 million managed endpoints showed that 63% of endpoints run more than one remote access tool, which can unnecessarily increase a company’s attack surface.
  • RDP was the most commonly abused remote access protocol in the dataset, with attackers enabling it through registry changes, disabling Network Level Authentication, using RDPWrap for concurrent sessions, and extracting saved RDP passwords.
  • ConnectWise ScreenConnect has been targeted through vulnerability exploitation such as CVE-2024-1709 and through trojanized installers that connect victims to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
  • MeshAgent was the single most frequently attacker-deployed tool in the dataset, and organizations that do not use MeshCentral are advised to treat any MeshAgent presence as a confirmed indicator of compromise.
  • The article recommends a tiered control approach: block tools such as MeshAgent and Ammyy Admin unless explicitly authorized, monitor and harden tools such as VNC, RDP, Tactical RMM, and Action1, and audit and maintain mainstream tools such as ScreenConnect, AnyDesk, TeamViewer, and Splashtop.

Cloudflare is launching early access to Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation, a Managed Defense service that uses OpenAI Daybreak models to find, validate, prioritize, and propose fixes for vulnerabilities in customer-authorized code. The key value is combining source-code analysis with Cloudflare production traffic, WAF, and security-event context so teams can focus first on exposed, actively targeted issues while retaining control over any patches or rules.

  • Cloudflare announced early access to Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation, an invitation-only service within Cloudflare Managed Defense that helps customers detect and mitigate vulnerabilities in authorized codebases.
  • The service uses OpenAI Daybreak models, including GPT-5.6 Cyber, for reconnaissance, hunting, and validation, while customers decide whether proposed code patches or mitigations are implemented.
  • Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation combines source code analysis with Cloudflare Web Assets, WAF, Workers Observability, and traffic and security data to prioritize findings based on production exposure and security activity.
  • The system can recommend code patches and, when evidence supports it, Cloudflare WAF Custom rules scoped around the method, path, and request details needed to reach vulnerable code.
  • Model prompts are sent from Cloudflare Workers through Cloudflare AI Gateway to OpenAI servers, and no model inference runs at Cloudflare's edge or can directly apply patches or rules.

A New Era for Offensive Security — Optional

NetSPI and Synack are merging, backed by KKR, to create a larger offensive security platform combining expert human testing with AI-enabled capabilities. The key message is that effective modern pentesting requires both automation and skilled judgment, not fully autonomous tools alone.

  • The companies cite nearly 40 years of combined operating history and more than 13 million hours of real-world offensive testing experience.
  • The article argues that fully autonomous testing falls short because complex vulnerabilities often require human judgment to identify, validate, and prioritize.
  • NetSPI and Synack say their combined approach will pair security talent with AI-enabled capabilities to deliver more sophisticated testing at greater scale.
  • The merged company plans to offer continuous security testing and validation across the full attack surface, expanded service offerings, and greater operational scale.

While anti-bot vendors talk about AI agents, classical bots are getting the bypasses — Optional

The article argues that the security industry is over-focusing on AI agent management while traditional bots are still successfully bypassing anti-bot systems. AI’s more immediate impact is helping attackers reverse engineer defenses and build faster, more scalable automation, so vendors should be judged on whether they can still detect purpose-built bots.

  • The article argues that AI agent management is not the same problem as traditional bot detection, anti-abuse, or fraud prevention.
  • The author says many major anti-bot systems are actively reverse engineered and bypassed by bot developers in Discord servers, Telegram groups, Reddit communities, and GitHub repositories.
  • The article states that attackers can generate valid anti-bot payloads without running protected JavaScript in a real browser, use browserless solvers, and solve CAPTCHAs at scale in well under a second.
  • The author argues that AI is helping attackers analyze undocumented public APIs, inspect and deobfuscate anti-bot JavaScript, debug automation, reproduce expected signals, and maintain their tools when targets change.
  • The article says anti-bot products should be judged by measurable outcomes such as fraudulent accounts created, credential stuffing that reaches login endpoints, emergency rules deployed, and automated traffic that bypasses defenses.

Supply Chain Attacks in 2026: Why Threat Intelligence Is the Only Early Warning System That Works — Optional

Supply chain attacks are now a major breach vector because trusted vendors, software components, and managed platforms can be compromised outside an organization’s direct visibility. The article argues that continuous external threat intelligence and vendor monitoring are necessary to detect these risks before they become public breaches.

  • Verizon's 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report found third-party involvement in 48% of breaches, up 60% year over year.
  • The article says supply chain attacks target vendors, software components, and build pipelines that an organization depends on, rather than attacking the organization directly.
  • CISA and the FBI documented that the Cl0p ransomware group exploited CVE-2023-34362 in Progress Software's MOVEit Transfer platform beginning on May 27, 2023.
  • By January 2024, breaches or downstream exposures linked to MOVEit affected more than 2,700 organizations and compromised personal data of more than 93 million people, according to tracking by Emsisoft and KonBriefing Research.
  • The article argues that continuous monitoring of vendor infrastructure, exposed credentials, dark web chatter, and third-party breach signals is needed because traditional vulnerability management does not cover those external risks.

The story behind the intelligence — Optional

Cisco Talos warns that AI model guardrails are increasingly blocking legitimate security work, creating a “safety penalty” that slows defenders while attackers use less-restricted tools. Security teams should measure AI refusal rates and plan fallback or private AI options to preserve incident-response capability.

  • The newsletter emphasizes that producing usable threat intelligence involves messy investigative work, including dead ends, conversations, and evidence-gathering that are usually abstracted away from the final product.
  • Talos researcher Azim Khodjibaev’s adversary engagement work includes developing deep- and dark-web personas, directly engaging threat actors, and maintaining relationships with people who have openly threatened him.
  • Khodjibaev has maintained eight separate personas at once, some of which interacted with one another, and his engagements have helped Talos identify prolific cybercriminals and support wider disruption efforts.
  • Cisco Talos describes an AI “safety penalty,” where built-in guardrails in frontier AI models increasingly block legitimate defensive tasks and can delay incident response.
  • Talos recommends that security leaders audit AI refusal rates and evaluate alternatives such as private infrastructure, Model-as-a-Service platforms, or hybrid fallback systems that reroute refused prompts to an unconstrained local model.

item.title: Python NodeStealer Evolves Into AI-Assisted Spyware With Telegram C2
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 18:00 → 02 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Python NodeStealer: AI-Assisted to Full Spyware — Should Read

Netskope researchers report that Python NodeStealer has evolved from a Facebook/browser infostealer into full spyware with keylogging, clipboard monitoring, screenshots, Wi-Fi and picture theft, and expanded Facebook Graph API harvesting. The new variant also uses split Telegram C2 channels and shows signs that its added capabilities were AI-assisted.

  • Netskope Threat Labs found an August 2026 Python NodeStealer variant with full spyware capabilities, including keystroke logging, clipboard monitoring, screenshot capture, and a dual Telegram bot command-and-control architecture.
  • The latest NodeStealer variant expands its theft targets to include Wi-Fi passwords, the victim’s Pictures folder, and two additional web browsers.
  • The new variant queries more than 20 Facebook Graph API endpoints covering identity, social graph, account security, advertising, and commerce data, compared with two endpoints in earlier variants.
  • Netskope Threat Labs observed indicators that newly added NodeStealer functions may have been AI-assisted, including systematic use of decorative emojis in output logs that was absent from previous variants.
  • The campaign’s victims were mainly in Asia and North America across multiple segments, with the financial services sector most represented.

item.title: CVE-2026-81891 elFinder ZIP Extraction MIME Bypass Enables Remote Code Execution
item.content:encoded:
Window: 02 Sep 14:00 → 02 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-81891) elFinder Remote Code Execution via ZIP Extraction MIME Bypass — Should Read

CVE-2026-81891 is a high-severity elFinder flaw that can let attackers achieve remote code execution by uploading and extracting ZIP archives containing PHP-executable files that bypass MIME checks. Organizations should upgrade to elFinder 2.1.70, restrict connector access, and block PHP execution in upload/extraction directories.

  • CVE-2026-81891 is an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in Studio 42 elFinder that can allow remote code execution through archive extraction.
  • The flaw occurs because checkExtractItems() calls mimetypeInternalDetect() without normalizing the detected MIME type, allowing PHP-executable extensions such as .phtml, .phar, .php5, and .php3 to bypass the uploadDeny filter.
  • All elFinder releases prior to 2.1.70 are affected, and version 2.1.70 fixes the MIME validation gap during archive extraction.
  • Affected assets are typically PHP web applications that embed elFinder as a file browser or media manager, often inside CMSs, admin panels, e-commerce back offices, customer portals, and internal file-sharing tools.
  • Recommended actions include inventorying elFinder deployments, restricting connector access, disabling archive extraction where unnecessary, blocking PHP execution in upload and extraction directories, and monitoring for unexpected PHP-executable files or requests.

Technologies: cms, web-server

Products: elfinder, cycognito-platform

Vendors: studio-42, cycognito

Gaming the system: how a Chinese-speaking actor turned Brazilian government sites into an SEO weapon — Must Read

Check Point Research says a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group linked to Earth Berberoka is compromising Brazilian government and education web servers, installing malicious Apache modules that turn trusted domains into stealth proxies for gambling-themed fake app-store pages and SEO manipulation. The same scalable infrastructure and Linux malware toolkit could be quickly repurposed from search fraud to direct malware delivery.

  • Check Point Research tracked a sustained campaign since mid-2025 against Brazilian organizations, primarily government and educational institutions, by a Chinese-speaking cybercrime cluster it calls Gambling Goblin.
  • The attackers install malicious Apache modules on compromised web servers to reverse-proxy selected visitors to attacker-controlled phishing pages while the traffic appears to come from the legitimate domain.
  • The phishing pages impersonate trusted app-distribution platforms such as Google Play, Microsoft Store, and Amazon while promoting online gambling and sports betting to Brazilian users.
  • The group deploys a heavily obfuscated Linux toolkit that includes DownPro, AlphaAgent, oRAT, a 3snake-based credential stealer, an SSH brute-forcer, and reconnaissance tools.
  • Check Point Research found related phishing networks localized in Vietnamese, Spanish, and English, as well as infrastructure that generates fresh domains daily.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, remote-access, cloud-platform

Products: apache-http-server, google-play, microsoft-store, amazon-appstore, bing, grpc

Vendors: apache-software-foundation, google, microsoft, amazon, cloudflare

Fully Signed, Fully Passed: The Reply-To Was the Payload — Should Read

A genuine European government mailbox sent a fully authenticated phishing email whose only payload was a hidden Reply-To diversion to an attacker-controlled address. Because DKIM, DMARC, and ARC all passed, the key lesson is that email authentication proves origin and integrity, not whether the reply path is safe.

  • A senior executive at a professional certification and credentialing organization received a one-line RFQ follow-up email from a genuine mailbox at a European regional government body.
  • The message had no link or attachment and used a Reply-To field containing both an attacker-controlled address, infodesk@frontdesk-investment[.]com, and the genuine government mailbox.
  • The government domain’s valid DKIM signature explicitly covered the Reply-To header, showing the covert reply address was present before the sending organization’s outbound gateway signed the message.
  • The email passed DKIM twice, DMARC, ARC, and Microsoft’s composite authentication verdict, demonstrating that the message was not forged even though its reply path was redirected.
  • The article says the practical control is to surface reply-path divergence during triage, especially when an inbound message’s reply domain does not match the From domain or contains multiple reply addresses.

item.content:encoded:

UK Cybercrime Journal: ExfilSquad Emerges — Must Read

ExfilSquad is targeting UK public sector, education, and law enforcement organizations with data-theft-only extortion, exploiting exposed SaaS, CRM, and Microsoft Power Pages configurations rather than deploying ransomware. The key risk is that misconfigured cloud-facing business portals can leak large volumes of sensitive contact and administrative data, which the group then distributes via torrents to increase pressure on victims.

  • In mid-2026, the cybercriminal group ExfilSquad launched an extortion campaign targeting prominent UK organizations across the public sector, education, and law enforcement, as well as other firms worldwide.
  • ExfilSquad operates as a pure data extortion group that steals data and threatens to publish it on its onion-based Data Leak Site if a ransom is not paid, rather than deploying encryptors or destructive malware.
  • The UK Department for Education, the Police National Legal Database, and Newcastle University confirmed breaches linked to ExfilSquad involving hundreds of thousands of records and, in the PNLD case, data affecting over 100,000 police officers, staff, and criminal justice professionals.
  • Analysis of ExfilSquad’s leak site details indicated that its primary attack vector involves exploiting misconfigurations in cloud portals, CRM platforms, internal case management systems, and publicly accessible Microsoft Power Pages data tables.
  • ExfilSquad uploaded multi-gigabyte torrent files for each victim to its TOR leak site and assigned distinct Torrent Trackers and initial Web Seeds per victim.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database

Products: microsoft-power-pages, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Vendors: microsoft, salesforce, snowflake, salesloft

Policy on Paper, Risk in Practice — Optional

Most organizations have AI data security policies, but fewer than one in 10 can enforce them consistently in real time across AI tools. The key risk is that sensitive data now moves through prompts, copy-paste, and AI-generated outputs faster than traditional file-based controls can track or block.

  • Nearly half of surveyed organizations still rely on written policies, post-event monitoring, or inconsistently enforced controls as their primary approach to data security enforcement.
  • Only 11% of organizations enforce data protection policies in real time across most environments, and only 8% do so for AI tools specifically.
  • Although 67% of organizations maintain a formal AI policy, fewer than one in 10 enforce it consistently in AI environments.
  • Most data protection architectures were built for files, while sensitive information increasingly moves through prompts, AI-generated summaries, and copy-pasted excerpts.
  • Only one in five organizations can apply consistent policy to prompt and text submissions into AI tools, and fewer than one in ten can recognize sensitive data once it has been modified, reformatted, or partially copied.

Machinery Cybersecurity Compliance EU Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 — Optional

Radiflow is promoting services to help machinery manufacturers and integrators prepare for the EU Machinery Regulation, which will make cybersecurity part of CE marking requirements from 20 January 2027. The key takeaway is to begin assessment, remediation, and documentation early to avoid compliance delays.

  • From 20 January 2027, cybersecurity becomes part of the Essential Health and Safety Requirements for industrial machinery for the first time.
  • The new cybersecurity requirements will make cybersecurity a legal precondition for CE marking and market access across Europe.
  • Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 enters into force on 20 January 2027.
